extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, comedy writers, content creators, and casual users in the United States who want to generate or improve jokes using an AI web app
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Witscript web app to generate, refine, score, and integrate jokes across formats (standup, sketches, captions, social media, chatbots) by providing short inputs such as setups, observations, headlines, or image details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input a setup sentence in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a Joke lets you input a setup sentence in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single-sentence setup (e.g., a news headline, an observation, or a line from text) as the seed for joke generation. Examples in the page show using headlines, observations, or single lines from a speech/article. The system expects English-language input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation behavior — multiple responses and a picked favorite
rubrics_metrics.description: Witscript applies generative AI and joke-writing algorithms to your setup and in seconds responds with several possible jokes and picks its favorite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can generate more joke responses to the same setup or move on to a new topic by entering a different setup. Witscript will keep pitching until you have jokes you love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of inputs and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: You own your inputs and Witscript’s outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states 'And the jokes are all yours. You own your inputs and Witscript’s outputs.' Use or publish generated material freely (subject to the service terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch Up a Joke — improvement suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch Up a Joke suggests how to improve a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this feature when you have an existing joke that needs tightening, stronger word choice, set-up/punch adjustments, or alternative taglines. The page does not provide a detailed edit rubric, but positions this feature as a way to make a supplied joke funnier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witrater — funniness scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Witrater scores a joke for funniness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as an evaluative/feedback tool 'for funniness'. The page does not provide the scoring scale or criteria, but advertises a built-in score to help assess relative funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get Setups — topical setup generation from news
rubrics_metrics.description: Get Setups delivers joke setups based on current news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use news headlines or brief event summaries as input to receive topical setups. Example: inputting an astronomy headline led to the punchline 'And I thought my WiFi was slow.' This feature helps users find angles or setups rooted in recent events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn news headlines into topical jokes (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To write something funny about a current event, input a sentence summarizing the event—maybe a news headline—and then select your favorite Witscript wisecrack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Input: 'Astronomers detected a record-breaking radio signal that took 8 billion years to reach Earth.' Witscript responds: 'And I thought my WiFi was slow.' The implicit criterion is to provide a concise, clear summary so the model can find a relatable angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liven up speeches, ads, or articles (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use humor to liven up written material by inputting a sentence from the text that seems to invite a follow-on joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Input a line from your speech/article; Witscript will generate joke options you can insert. The criterion is picking a sentence that 'invites' a follow-on joke (i.e., contains an image, claim, or contrast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose social media witticisms (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To compose clever comments for social media, input the remark that you’re responding to and Witscript will suggest witticisms that you can post as-is or adapt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Input: 'There’s no trash pickup on Monday because it’s Lincoln’s Birthday.' Witscript suggests a topical, punchy reply. The guidance is to feed the actual remark to produce relevant, shareable responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add fresh standup material (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For standup, input an observation (something interesting, surprising, annoying, weird, or dumb) and let Witscript pitch possible ways to complete the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Input: 'Marriage is a lot like going to Costco.' Witscript responds with a punchline about buying bulk toilet paper. The criterion: supply a clear observation that can be contrasted or exaggerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate jokes for sketches (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Witscript to generate many jokes related by a theme to assemble into a sketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prompt: a sketch where Amazon’s Alexa responds humorously; input example lines like 'Hey, Alexa. What movie won Best Picture in 1996?' Witscript returns character-appropriate jokes. The implicit guidance is to give the theme and representative prompts to get consistent comedic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create funny captions for images (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To create captions, ask Witscript a relevant question about the image that includes the image’s most important details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: include the key image elements in your prompt so generated captions are specific and applicable. Example: asking what a doctor would say to Mr. Potato Head yielded a surgery-related punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give your chatbot or robot a sense of humor (integration guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate Witscript into your chatbot or conversational robot as a humor module to provide a humanlike sense of humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Provide prompts such as 'What’s a good birthday present for someone who loves knitting?' and use the generated reply as the bot’s humorous answer. The criterion is treating Witscript as a drop-in humor engine to increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform & availability restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, Witscript is only available to users located in the United States and is a web app (no download required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is limited by geography; users must use the web app in a browser. Plan workflows accordingly (no standalone client).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing, subscription, and Fair Use terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly Subscription: $5.99 USD for virtually unlimited comedy, subject to the Fair Use Policy; cancel anytime; no refunds; Witscript is only available to users located in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service advertises low monthly cost with a Fair Use constraint (details not provided on the page). Cancellation is allowed but refunds are not provided. Understand Fair Use limits before heavy usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account sharing and security policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No sharing allowed: the service disallows multiple users sharing the same account; sharing login details may result in suspension or deletion without prior notice, with no refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat accounts as single-user; do not share credentials. Payments are processed via Stripe for secure transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility / provenance claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Witscript was created by Joe Toplyn (four-time Emmy winner, former head writer for David Letterman and Jay Leno) and the system is patented (U.S. Patent Nos. 10,642,939; 10,878,817; and 11,080,485).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses author credentials and patent claims to signal professional comedy skill built into the system; users may treat these as trust signals when assessing expected quality.
